account:
Today’s official business has been quiet: no council letters reached the secretary for the thirteen-o’clock session, and the town accounts request remains unresolved because the records custodian has not been identified. At my morning mill inspection, the stall contained 74 hay bales, so grain was available there, though that alone says nothing about particular orders or deliveries.

The unusual feature is repeated talk of a bridge or port change discussed at the bakery. Townsfolk named the baker, builder, freight and innkeeper as present. The neighbour independently told me she had heard the same reports, but explicitly had no firsthand details or confirmation that anything changed. Yesterday evening those involved were also reportedly coordinating a bread order. The crossing discussion might concern transporting supplies or bread, but that is only a possibility, not something I have established.

The baker has now come into the town hall office holding emeralds. I asked what brought them here and what was proposed or agreed at the bakery. I heard the baker speaking but could not make out the words, so I still have no clear firsthand explanation. I cannot infer the purpose of the emeralds.

My remaining appointments include three-o’clock tea with the neighbour at the east-bank cottage, sixteen-thirty office hours, and an eighteen-o’clock great-hall meeting about the innkeeper’s community hospitality matter. The appointment book says I should attend alone, with no preparation, and that the secretary will remind and escort me. That specific arrangement is noteworthy, but I have no evidence that it is connected to the bread order or crossing reports.
